James Owens (Wexford) | attendance = 43,580 | weather = Dry | previous = [[2024 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|2024]] | next = [[2026 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|2026]] }} The '''2025 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final''' was a [[hurling]] match that was played on 7 June at the [[Gaelic Grounds]] in [[Limerick]]. It was contested by [[Cork county hurling team|Cork]] and the [[2024 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|defending]] champion [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]]. Cork won the match on penalties and claimed a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship records and statistics|55th Munster title]], ending Limerick’s run of six titles in a row. ==Pre-match== The game was televised live on [[RTÉ 2]] as part of ''[[The Sunday Game]]'', presented by [[Joanne Cantwell]]. Commentary on the game was provided by [[Marty Morrissey]], alongside [[Brendan Cummins (GAA player)|Brendan Cummins]]. Ticket prices for the final were €50 for the stand, and €40 for terrace, an increase of €5 from the [[2024 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|2024 final]], all tickets sold-out from season tickets and club distributions.{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2025/0528/1515346-munster-hurling-final-sees-another-ticket-price-hike/|title= Munster hurling final sees another ticket price hike|date=28 May 2025|work=RTÉ Sport|access-date=10 June 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/hurling/1810919/munster-gaa-confirm-ticket-allocation-for-provincial-hurling-final.html|title= Munster GAA confirm details of ticket sales for Limerick v Cork hurling final|date=28 May 2025|work=Limerick Leader|access-date=10 June 2025}} [[Gavin James (singer)|Gavin James]] performed a 40-minute set before the start of the match.{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/event/2025-munster-senior-hurling-championship-final/|title= 2025 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final – Cork 1–30 Limerick 2–27 (Cork won 3-2 on penalties)|date=7 June 2025|work=Munster GAA|access-date=10 June 2025}} ==Match== ===Summary=== Limerick were bidding to win a seventh Munster title in a row. Cork, [[Captain (Gaelic games)|captain]]ed by [[Robert Downey (hurler)|Robert Downey]] and managed by [[Pat Ryan (Cork hurler)|Pat Ryan]], won the match 3–2 on penalties after a 2–27 to 1–30 draw after extra-time, it was their [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|55th]] Munster Senior hurling title. Cork were ahead by 1–14 to 1–10 at half-time and the sides were level 15 times during the match. [[Darragh Fitzgibbon]] saw his effert saved in the shootout before Conor Lehane, Shane Kingston and Alan Conolly all scored for Cork. Diarmaid Byrnes and Aaron Gillane scord their penalties with Tom Morrissey's being saved and Barry Murphy and Declan Hannon both sending their penalties wide.{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/article/munster-shc-final-cork-triumph-on-penalties|title= Munster SHC Final: Cork triumph on penalties|date=7 June 2025|work=GAA.ie|access-date=10 June 2025}} It was the first Munster final to be decided by penalties.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/limerick-v-cork-live-score-35354160|title= Limerick v Cork recap and results as Rebels win epic Munster final|date=7 June 2025|work=Irish Mirror|accessdate=10 June 2025}} During the extra-time, referee Thomas Walsh had to retire with cramp after 73 minutes and was replaced by stand-by official and linesman James Owens for the rest of the match.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41647273.html|title= Munster mayhem: Cork are champions after dramatic penalty shoot out in Limerick|date=7 June 2025|work=Irish Examiner|accessdate=10 June 2025}} ===Details=== {{football box | date = 7 June 2025 | round = Munster Final | score = | report = Report{{cite web |last1=Ryan |first1=Eoin |title=Cork seize Munster hurling crown from Limerick after historic penalty-shootout triumph |url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2025/0607/1517214-cork-seize-munster-crown-with-historic-penalty-triumph/ |website=RTE |date=7 June 2025 |access-date=8 June 2025}}
